summary: A bounded persistent native T2 session built the 91.5M-parameter model once, loaded the unchanged adapter once, completed two authenticated assignments, and reduced warm cache-validation plus runtime-initialization time from 2.9631700000027195 seconds to 0.00004199999966658652 seconds (99.9985826%) while preserving zero warm immutable-state payload, 2.1866353039878446e-7 checkpoint relative L2, and the one-shot held-out improvement.

guardrails.detail: The persistent checkpoint relative L2 was 2.1866353039878446e-7, identical to the one-shot profile and below 1e-6.
Held-out mean loss improved by 0.0033478736877441406, matching the one-shot T2 checkpoint.
The reused second assignment reported zero model and adapter payload bytes.
Exact-tree tests and an adversarial probe showed shape and conversion failures mutate no adapter parameter, leave the old digest intact, and permit old-digest reuse only with the complete old state.

findings.label: Persistent reuse removes one-shot setup
findings.description: Warm cache validation and runtime initialization fell by 99.9985826%; setup was 0.0025% of gradient-compute time instead of dominating it.

findings.label: Persistent lifecycle leaves trajectory unchanged
findings.description: The adapter/checkpoint identities, numerical parity, and held-out result exactly matched the one-shot T2 profile.

findings.label: Persistent reuse does not reduce resident memory
findings.description: Peak process RSS remained about 1.746GB because the complete FP32 model stays resident. Quantized placement is still required for the next memory reduction.

findings.label: One worker can fill multiple shards
findings.description: This throughput profile intentionally lets one allowlisted worker complete both sequential shards; it does not demonstrate participant diversity or independent-failure redundancy.

limitations: The proof ran on one Windows host over loopback and does not measure WAN scheduling or remote participant churn.
One worker ID completed both assignments; campaigns requiring contributor diversity need a separate admission/quorum policy.
The T2 base is deterministic and randomly initialized; the held-out improvement is a guardrail, not useful language-model quality.
The model remains complete FP32 CPU residency and does not prove quantization, GPU placement, mapped storage, or larger-than-RAM execution.
Failure atomicity covers validation and conversion before copy; catastrophic device failure during the final same-shape copy phase is outside this proof.
Retry after a lost HTTP receipt and partial completion of a requested --assignments count was reasoned through but not separately fault-injected.
